user.title: Energy provider
user.description:
KD Helios prices your energy with the live tariff of your own provider. Prices come from [epexprijzen.nl](https://epexprijzen.nl) and already include VAT, energy tax and the provider charge.

Choose your provider and whether your tariff changes every hour or every quarter.

data_description.provider: The provider as listed on epexprijzen.nl. It must offer a dynamic contract.
data_description.price_interval: Most dynamic contracts settle per quarter hour. Pick hourly only if your contract does.

reconfigure.description: Change the provider or the price interval. Existing devices and their totals are kept.

user.title: Add a device
user.description:
Track what one appliance or circuit actually costs by attaching an existing power or energy entity.

An energy entity (kWh) is preferred because it is exact. A power entity (W) is integrated over time and is a good fallback for plugs that only report power.

Use **Add EV charger** instead when the device is a charger: that workflow also asks about employer reimbursement and ERE certificates.

data_description.name: The name shown in Home Assistant, for example "Heat pump" or "Washing machine".
data_description.power_entity: A sensor in W or kW that reports current power.
data_description.energy_entity: A cumulative sensor in kWh. Takes precedence over the power entity.

reconfigure.title: Edit device
reconfigure.description: Change the name or the entity this device is metered from. Its totals are preserved.

data_description.power_entity: A sensor in W or kW that reports current power.
data_description.energy_entity: A cumulative sensor in kWh. Takes precedence over the power entity.

error.no_source: Attach a power entity, an energy entity, or both.
error.duplicate_source: The power and energy entity must be different sensors.

user.title: Grid connection
user.description:
Point KD Helios at your meter so the whole connection is costed, not only the devices you track.

Pick your meter below and KD Helios will look up its import and export counters on the next screen. Leave it empty to select the counters yourself.

data_description.meter_device: For example your HomeWizard P1 meter, DSMR reader or other energy meter.
data_description.saldering: Net exported kWh against imported kWh within the calendar year, so an exported kWh is worth the import tariff. It switches off by itself on 1 January 2027, when saldering ends.

entities.title: Meters
entities.description:
Counters found on **{meter}**: {detected}.

Check them before continuing. The import counter is required; export and the power sensors are optional.

data_description.import_entity: Cumulative kWh taken from the grid.
data_description.export_entity: Cumulative kWh returned to the grid. Leave empty if you never export.
data_description.import_power_entity: Optional live power, in W or kW.
data_description.export_power_entity: Optional live export power, in W or kW.
data_description.grid_power_entity: One sensor that reports net power: positive when importing, negative when exporting. The import and export power sensors are derived from its sign. A P1 meter usually has exactly one of these.

tariff.title: Feed-in and fixed costs
tariff.description:
epexprijzen.nl does not publish feed-in data through its API, so the suggested value comes from its own provider dataset, read on {snapshot}.

**{provider}**: a deduction of **{suggested}** EUR/kWh. A negative amount means the provider pays a bonus on top of the spot price.

Check it against your contract and confirm it. A wrong deduction distorts every euro of export revenue.

user.title: Home battery
user.description:
KD Helios works out **when** charging your battery is most profitable, using the same tariff it already tracks: buy in the cheap hours, and let the battery discharge into the expensive ones.

Give it the battery's SOC sensor plus its real capacity and charge power. With writes enabled it can also program the six time-of-use slots of a Deye inverter through the Solarman integration.

data_description.soc_entity: The battery state of charge, for example the Solarman battery SOC sensor.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Total usable battery capacity in kWh, not the inverter's rating.
data_description.max_charge_kw: How fast the battery can charge. Used to spread a window over several slots.
data_description.reserve_soc: Never plan to discharge below this. The inverter's idle slots use it too.
data_description.target_soc: Only buy energy up to this state of charge.
data_description.efficiency: Round-trip efficiency. 90 percent means a stored kWh returns 0.9 kWh.
data_description.battery_horizon_hours: How far ahead to look for a cheaper hour to discharge into. Battery prices cover today and tomorrow.
data_description.inverter_device: The Solarman inverter device, required before writes can be enabled.
data_description.allow_inverter_writes: Off by default. Writes change how your battery behaves and must be triggered explicitly.

reconfigure.description: Change the battery parameters or the write settings.

user.title: Add an EV charger
user.description:
Attach the power or energy entity of the charger. An energy entity (kWh) is preferred because it is exact.

The next two steps ask about employer reimbursement and ERE certificates, which only apply to charging.

data_description.name: The name shown in Home Assistant, for example "EV charger".
data_description.power_entity: A sensor in W or kW that reports current power.
data_description.energy_entity: A cumulative sensor in kWh. Takes precedence over the power entity.

reimbursement.title: Employer reimbursement
reimbursement.description:
When your employer pays for charging, every kWh earns money back.

**Fixed** pays a set amount per kWh.

**Dynamic** follows the formula `(market price + fixed surcharge) × surcharge percentage`. With a percentage of 100 that is simply `market price + surcharge`.

data_description.reimbursement_mode: No reimbursement, a fixed rate, or the dynamic formula.
data_description.reimbursement_rate: Amount your employer pays per kWh, in euros.
data_description.reimbursement_surcharge: Fixed amount added to the market price, in euros per kWh.
data_description.reimbursement_percent: Multiplier applied after the surcharge. 100 means no extra margin, 105 adds five percent.
data_description.reimbursement_basis: EPEX spot excludes VAT and energy tax. All-in is what you pay at home.
data_description.reimbursement_interval: How often the tariff your employer uses changes. Choose per hour when the reimbursement settles hourly while your own contract settles per quarter; the reimbursement then uses the hour average instead of the quarter hour price.

ere.title: ERE certificates
ere.description:
ERE certificates add value to every kWh you charge.

**Fixed** values each kWh at `ERE per kWh × price per ERE`.

**Joulo** derives the ERE per kWh from the cumulative Joulo counters, so it follows what the charger actually earns.

data_description.ere_mode: No ERE value, a fixed ratio, or the Joulo integration.
data_description.ere_per_kwh: Also used as the fallback while a Joulo ratio is not available yet.
data_description.ere_price: Value of one ERE certificate in euros.
data_description.ere_price_entity: Optional sensor with the live price per ERE, for example the Joulo market price sensor.
data_description.ere_credits_entity: Cumulative ERE credits, for example sensor.joulo_total_ere_credits.
data_description.ere_kwh_entity: Cumulative charged energy, for example sensor.joulo_total_all_kwh.

reconfigure.title: Edit EV charger
reconfigure.description: Change any setting of this charger. Its totals, including the energy already priced, are preserved.

data_description.reimbursement_basis: EPEX spot excludes VAT and energy tax. All-in is what you pay at home.
data_description.reimbursement_interval: How often the tariff your employer uses changes, independently of your own contract.
data_description.ere_per_kwh: Also used as the fallback while a Joulo ratio is not available yet.

no_devices.title: KD Helios is not tracking any device yet
no_devices.description:
The tariff is loaded, but nothing is being metered yet.

Go to **Settings → Devices & services → KD Helios** and choose **Add device** to attach a power or energy entity to an appliance, a circuit or an EV charger.

Until you do, KD Helios only shows the current energy prices.
